conviction_note: One clean fact: after seven sessions pinned in a two-cent band below $1, Waterdrop traded 1,676,400 shares on 2026-09-04 - 6.6x its 20-day average and eight times the prior session - and closed back above $1.00 on the last day before the print, with no filing and nothing in the capture to explain it; that is buying, but this name's eight prior reactions span -3.33% to +2.68% so the number has to be small.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-04, the last session before the print, WDH traded 1,676,400 shares against a 254,685 20-day average and 201,700 the day before - 6.6x average, 8.3x the prior session and by far the heaviest day of the run-in - and closed at $1.02, back above the $1.00 mark after seven consecutive closes below it ($0.994, $0.995, $0.995, $0.993, $0.985, $0.976, $0.973 on 8/25 to 9/2, a two-cent band on 138,800-208,300 shares); nothing in the capture explains it - the last filing of any kind was a 6-K accepted 2026-07-24T20:01:08Z and the only commentary in the window is three StockTwits posts.

findings.why_not_priced: A 20-day realised vol of 13.2% on a $1 Chinese ADS is the signature of a stock being held in place, and the shareholder record says exactly that on 2026-08-10: 'looks almost like the price is being prevented from falling below $1'. A single 1.68m-share session that breaks the pin upward on the eve of the print is either an accumulator or the company's own bid defending the NYSE $1 threshold before releasing results; either way it is one-directional flow that no news, no filing and no aggregator has attached a reason to. If it were priced there would be a filing or a captured item, and there is neither - the news channel returned zero items for this name across all ten sweeps.
findings.independence: One supporting datapoint from a different source, and it is weak: a post of 2026-09-03T11:03:30Z in the same digest says 'Market share rising: GSE market share increased to 15%', which is the only company-specific claim anywhere in the run-in window and which I could not trace to a company release. Nothing else in this corpus points the same way. none.

any Chinese insurance-regulation or channel datapoint for the June quarter
baseline_tension: It sits with the run-in rather than against it: +2.72% over five days and +2.0% over twenty, most of it delivered in the single 09-04 session, on a name 48.7% below its 52-week high and 4.8% above its low - so I am reading the last session as the signal rather than the whole drift.
corpus_limits: On the harness question: the session classification for this event looks right - the sealed 6-K (accession 0001104659-26-105667) was accepted 2026-09-08T11:30:46Z, i.e. 07:30 ET, squarely pre-market - but the reaction history it sits on is not clean, and in two identifiable ways. First, three of the eight matched filings carry session_conflict flags. Second, and worse, the Q1 2026 results reached the tape on 2026-06-16 (the StockTwits recap is timestamped 2026-06-16T11:57:23Z and the transcript link is dated 2026-6-16), yet no 6-K appears in filings.json for that date; the baseline instead counts 2026-06-17 (+2.34%) and 2026-06-23 (-0.83%) as two separate prints, so for that quarter the exhibit-text path is measuring the day after the press release and double-counting. The 2026-07-24 6-K, accepted 16:01 ET and 46 days before this print, is almost certainly not an earnings release at all. The consequence is that the 1.73% median is computed partly over non-events and may understate the true reaction; I have still sized to it because I have nothing better. Otherwise: 54 items of which 52 are EDGAR index entries, no news channel, no filing body text, no option chain, no short interest, and the sweeps stop on 2026-09-07 - so there is no post-print snapshot and no 2026-09-08 bar in quote.json, and nothing post-print leaked into this capture at all.
